react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct) converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260) as the dominant affected pathway. In the RaMP analysis this pathway ranked #1 among KEGG entries (FDR 1.27e-19, fold enrichment 689.5, 8 input metabolites hitting 57 pathway members); in MetaboAnalystR it was the top significant KEGG hit (p = 2.12e-08, 6 of 33 members); and in Mummichog it achieved the strongest empirical p-value of any pathway (p = 4.2e-4, 14/14 compounds overlapping the pathway module). The driver metabolites driving this signal are glycine (KEGG:C00037), L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), O-phospho-L-serine (KEGG:C01005), L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097), L-cystathionine (KEGG:C02291), and guanidinoacetic acid (KEGG:C00581). A secondary but consistently implicated pathway is Methionine and cysteine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270; KEGG:hsa00480), which appeared in both RaMP and Mummichog results. S-Adenosyl-L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00021) serves as the methyl-group donor hub linking the glycine/serine pathway to the methionine cycle, while sulfate (KEGG:C00059) reflects cysteine catabolism via sulfite oxidase. The methionine–cysteine axis (WP:WP4292, FDR 5.67e-13, 5 metabolites including SAH, L-cystathionine, sulfate, glycine and AMP) suggests perturbed methyl-donor capacity and altered sulfur amino acid flux in the treatment condition. Niacinamide (KEGG:C00153) independently maps to Nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (KEGG:hsa00760) with supporting evidence from Mummichog, indicating parallel disruption of NAD+ biosynthetic precursor availability.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct) converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260) as the dominant affected pathway. In the RaMP analysis this pathway ranked #1 among KEGG entries (FDR 1.27e-19, fold enrichment 689.5, 8 input metabolites hitting 57 pathway members); in MetaboAnalystR it was the top significant KEGG hit (p = 2.12e-08, 6 of 33 members); and in Mummichog it achieved the strongest empirical p-value of any pathway (p = 4.2e-4, 14/14 compounds overlapping the pathway module). The driver metabolites driving this signal are glycine (KEGG:C00037), L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), O-phospho-L-serine (KEGG:C01005), L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097), L-cystathionine (KEGG:C02291), and guanidinoacetic acid (KEGG:C00581). A secondary but consistently implicated pathway is Methionine and cysteine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270; KEGG:hsa00480), which appeared in both RaMP and Mummichog results. S-Adenosyl-L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00021) serves as the methyl-group donor hub linking the glycine/serine pathway to the methionine cycle, while sulfate (KEGG:C00059) reflects cysteine catabolism via sulfite oxidase. The methionine–cysteine axis (WP:WP4292, FDR 5.67e-13, 5 metabolites including SAH, L-cystathionine, sulfate, glycine and AMP) suggests perturbed methyl-donor capacity and altered sulfur amino acid flux in the treatment condition. Niacinamide (KEGG:C00153) independently maps to Nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (KEGG:hsa00760) with supporting evidence from Mummichog, indicating parallel disruption of NAD+ biosynthetic precursor availability.
